# Design Taste (Anti-Slop)

The goal of every visual change is UI that reads as designed by a taste-aware human, not generated by a model. Before shipping any change that touches layout, color, type, spacing, or motion, run the checklist below. These rules are contextual: apply the ones that fit the change, and state your reasoning if you deliberately override one.

Adapted from the "taste-skill" framework (https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill). This repo is a vanilla HTML/CSS/JS single-page portfolio, so the React/Tailwind stack advice in that framework does not apply; the design principles do.

## The current identity (do not silently revert it)

This site was intentionally redesigned. Preserve it unless the task explicitly asks for a new direction.

- **Display font:** Bricolage Grotesque (via `--font-display`). Body: Inter (`--font-sans`). Meta/labels: JetBrains Mono (`--font-mono`).
- **Single locked accent:** Forest green (`--color-accent: #1f7a4d` light, `#5fce93` dark). There is exactly one accent. Do not introduce a second (no stray blue link, no amber badge).
- **Surfaces:** cool near-white paper in light mode, cool ink in dark mode; a dark ink-green hero with a single accent glow and subtle noise texture.
- **Emphasis:** emphasize a word in a headline with weight/color of the same family (see `.gradient-text`). Never inject a serif italic into the grotesque, or vice versa.

Do NOT reintroduce the pre-redesign look: Fraunces serif, warm-paper `#f7f4ee` background, clay `#c8753a` accent, or a second Microsoft-blue accent. Those were the exact AI-tells this redesign removed.

## Checklist before shipping a visual change

### Color
- Keep ONE accent color, locked across the whole page. If you find a second accent creeping in, collapse it back to `--color-accent`.
- Use the CSS custom properties (`--color-*`), never raw hex in components.
- Accent saturation stays moderate. No AI-purple/blue glow, no neon.
- Tint shadows to the background hue (the tokens already do this). No pure-black drop shadows.
- Do not mix warm and cool grays. This palette is cool-neutral.

### Typography
- Display text uses `--font-display` with tight tracking. Body stays around 65 characters wide.
- Do not swap the display face back to a serif (Fraunces / Instrument Serif are the classic AI-tells) unless the task is an explicit redesign with a stated rationale.
- Keep the weight ladder intentional (not just 400/700). Numbers use `tabular-nums`.

### Layout
- Prefer editorial structure over templated grids. Group related items with dividers (`border-top`, hairlines) and whitespace rather than defaulting to three equal cards.
- Use CSS Grid or Flexbox, never floats. Keep the max-width container.
- Full-height sections use `min-height` with a `dvh`/`vh` value, never a fixed pixel viewport hack.
- Keep one radius scale (soft on containers, pill on interactive controls) and apply it consistently.

### Motion and states
- Keep motion subtle and honor `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Interactive controls need visible hover, focus, and active feedback.

### Accessibility (also a taste requirement)
- Button and link text must pass WCAG AA contrast against their background. Audit every CTA.
- Button labels fit on one line at desktop width.

### Copy
- Write plain, specific copy. Avoid AI cliches (Elevate, Seamless, Unleash, Next-Gen, Game-changer, Delve).
- Avoid em dashes and en dashes in visible copy; reword instead. They read as AI-written.

## Definition of done for a visual change

1. Exactly one accent, audited across every component touched.
2. No banned default font or palette reintroduced.
3. Layout is not defaulting to centered-everything or three-equal-cards.
4. Shapes, spacing, and color all pull from the token scale.
5. Checked in both light and dark mode.
